summary: Temporary elevated sudo for cross-team secondment and laptop ownership transfer — policy clarification
description:
Issue summary: HR requests guidance for a 10-working-day cross-team secondment where the engineer (temporary assignee) needs ephemeral elevated sudo on a shared internal lab machine and will physically take their primary laptop to a partner office for two weeks. We need clarity on: (1) allowed duration and approval path for temporary sudo; (2) the canonical owner of the laptop asset during a short-term location transfer (HR assigned vs receiving team); (3) required steps for KMS/credentials and service-account access while the device is offsite; (4) checklist items IT must perform before/after return to satisfy audit and asset tracking.

Impact: Policy ambiguity delaying secondment start (team is asking for green light). Potential risk to security posture if sudo is granted without timeboxed controls or if asset ownership/chain-of-custody is unclear for KMS/HSM access and corporate VPN requirements.

Background: The employee is a mid-level infra engineer on Platform (ID redacted). HR approved secondment to Partnerships team for knowledge transfer. Duration: two calendar weeks (10 working days). The employee will take their company-issued laptop offsite (partner office, EU region) and needs to run privileged maintenance on a lab host (internal-us-east shared GPU node) during the secondment window. Past tickets show ad-hoc short sudo grants have varied between 3 days and 2 weeks; security wants a more prescriptive flow.

Requested outcome: A concise, operational runbook we can follow for this case that answers approval path, minimum controls (MFA, Just-In-Time access, audit logging), device hand-off documentation, and any required key-rotation or service-account deactivation/rotation on return.
requested_actions: Confirm approved duration for temporary sudo/JIT access for a cross-team secondment
Specify approvers (HR + receiving manager + InfoSec?) and required Jira/Syslog entries
Confirm whether laptop ownership for a short transfer remains with HR (asset custody) or with receiving team, and which ticketing flow to use for chain-of-custody
List mandatory pre-departure IT checklist (disk encryption, latest patches, VPN config, recorded serial/asset tag, KMS access policy review)
List mandatory return checklist (credential rotation, device health scan, asset receipt acknowledgement, re-enrollment timeline)
Provide recommended Just-In-Time (JIT) mechanisms: ephemeral sudo via bastion, RBAC expiry, MFA enforcement, session recording/tracing endpoints
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Filing on behalf of HR (Rebecca L.) — we need to avoid delaying start date next Monday. Can SRE/InfoSec advise the minimal acceptable guardrails?

2026-03-10 - Marcus Chen (HR Ops): For short secondments we usually leave laptop ownership with HR but record receiving team in the asset ticket. Need confirmation if that remains policy-compliant for EU travel.

2026-03-11 - Lina Gomez (InfoSec): Do not grant open-ended sudo. Recommend JIT access via PAM with max 8 hours, renewal only with manager + security approval. Also require session recording for any root actions on prod-like hosts.

2026-03-11 - SRE Lead (Tom Reyes): The shared lab GPU node (internal-us-east) is in the 'non-prod' cluster but has access to KV-backed datasets. We can approve a scoped sudo for specific service accounts. Will need a PR to ops-config and an 'expiring' ACL in the gateway. Tom -> linking INT-365091 (prestage-onboarding script) for reference on automating ephemeral granting.
2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: HR requests a one-page checklist we can attach to the employee offer/secondment letter. Also: what to do should the employee be unable to return on schedule?

2026-03-12 - Security (J. O'Neill): If the device will travel to EU, ensure full-disk encryption is verified and endpoint DLP agent is active. If the device will connect to partner networks, require split-tunnel restrictions and corporate VPN mandatory with device posture checks. Recommend rotating any service account creds touched within 48 hours of return.
investigation_notes: Checked asset inventory: laptop serial 7C-XX-YY currently assigned to employee; last inventory confirmation 2025-11-04; warranty/MDM status OK
Reviewed past tickets for temporary sudo: patterns show 3-10 day grants with varying controls; no consistent JIT mechanism documented
Examined IAM policies: we have automated expiring keys for cloud roles but not for SSH sudo on internal lab hosts; ops-config PR template exists to add expiring ACLs

Checked legal/regulatory flag: travel to EU may trigger data transfer considerations depending on datasets accessed; partner office confirmed no sensitive datasets will be accessed, but confirm before granting KV access
resolution_notes: Pending InfoSec final approval and an ops-config PR to create an expiring ACL and session recording config. HR needs a short checklist doc to attach to secondment email. Target: produce checklist + ephemeral-sudo runbook by 2026-03-15.
